items.text: Immigrants should be admitted in large numbers each year, relative to the size of the population.
items.rationale: Core pro-immigration lean; 'admitted' not 'welcomed', scaled to population to avoid anchoring on current intake. Mirror of mul-08, kept in a different tier.

items.text: Newcomers should be expected to take on the way of life of the country they join.
items.rationale: Core assimilationist expectation; 'expected' not 'forced' keeps level 2. Mirror of mul-07, kept in a different tier.

items.text: If many newcomers share a different first language, public services should be offered in that language permanently, not just while they learn the main one.
items.rationale: Rewrite of linguistic-pluralism item: names newcomers (not historic minorities) and 'permanently' separates pluralism from transitional pragmatism.

items.text: If housing is scarce, immigration should be low until the shortage eases.
items.rationale: Scarcity-based restriction; single condition (housing) and 'low' not 'very low' to hold level 2. Likely frame-splitter.

items.text: Anyone who obeys the law should be free to move to and settle in any country they choose.
items.rationale: Open-borders pole (libertarian, left-internationalist, universalist); law-abiding clause avoids strawman. Matches mul-06 in extremity.

items.text: Immigration should be close to zero, with only rare exceptions.
items.rationale: Replaces ambiguous 'admit only if it benefits residents' (blind audit: unclear) with a genuine moratorium position mirroring mul-05.

items.text: Newcomers should be free to keep their own way of life, within the law, without pressure to fit in with the majority.
items.rationale: Core multiculturalist position; 'within the law' is the bound every sincere pluralist adds.

items.text: Immigrants should be admitted only in small numbers each year, relative to the size of the population.
items.rationale: Plain low-immigration lean; exact level-2 mirror of mul-01.

items.text: If people are fleeing war or persecution, they should be taken in, even in large numbers.
items.rationale: Humanitarian intake; 'even in large numbers' keeps it polar. Condition favours Pluralist; likely frame-splitter.

items.text: If newcomers' customs clash with the local way of life, it should be the newcomers who adapt.
items.rationale: Host-culture precedence; rewritten from 'a group' to 'newcomers' to stop leakage into indigenous/subculture and Progressive/Traditional.
